deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a page of German lecture notes on ancient Greek history, written in a Kurrent hand that may well be a student's notebook rather than Gauss's own work. It continues the previous page's account of the Theban hegemony.

Content, in order:
(1) Epaminondas and Pelopidas were the best of friends from youth until death.
(2) Pelopidas came from a very rich family; Epaminondas came from one of middling circumstances.
(3) Epaminondas: his whole life was a striving for higher perfection. His purity of morals was unmatched among his contemporaries. He was Greece's greatest general and its first tactical/military genius, but an even greater statesman than general.
(4) Pelopidas shared his convictions but had more outward pleasantness. He was the liberator of Thebes.
(5) Pelopidas was among the exiles. With about 40-50 men he surprised the city and drove out the whole Spartan garrison.
(6) Sparta sent an army to help its garrison, but it came too late. A duplicated phrase, 'aber zu spät kam', is struck through, apparently in red ink. So in 378 the Thebans won the citadel (the Cadmea).
(7) Open war between Sparta and Thebes now began.
(8) The Athenians sent help to Thebes, and Pelopidas... (continued on the next page).

There are no derivations, formulas or computations to reconstruct.
errors: Historical, not mathematical: the liberation of Thebes and the recapture of the Cadmea is conventionally dated to the winter of 379/378 BC. The note gives 378, which is acceptable as the Attic year 379/8.
Historical: Plutarch puts the core band of returning exiles at about 12. The '40-50' figure is a looser count of all participants. This is a minor discrepancy typical of lecture notes.

results.what: Lecture notes on Greek history (Epaminondas, Pelopidas, liberation of Thebes, 379/378 BC); no mathematical content
results.usually_credited_to: n/a (standard classical history, e.g. Plutarch, Xenophon, Diodorus)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only routine schoolbook ancient history with no mathematics. It is possibly not even in Gauss's hand: it looks like a student notebook bound into the bundle.
transcription_corrections: The line rendered as 'Darauf schickten die Spartaner nach Theben eine Armee zu Hülfe' appears in the image to read closer to 'Sparta schickte den Spartanern in Theben eine Armee zu Hülfe'. That reading makes better sense: Sparta sent relief to its garrison.
'Spartanische Besatzung' is written partly in the left margin, as a continuation of 'verjagte die ganze'.
'das erste kriegerische[?] Genie' may instead read 'das erste taktische Genie'. The word is uncertain.
The struck-through duplicate 'aber zu spät kam' is crossed out in red ink.
'mittlern Glücks umständen' should read 'mittlern Glücksumständen' (one word broken across the line).
